 Dodgers GM Brandon Gomes says the team will proceed “business as usual” and adjust as markets develop with a Dec. 1 labor deadline looming.
 The Dodgers are in contact with free-agent pitcher Tarik Skubal’s team and expects to meet with him.
 The team is searching for a Miguel Rojas replacement after his retirement.
 p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text" data-dateline data-subscriber-content> LAS VEGAS —  Standing outside of a packed conference room, half a day into baseball’s general manager meetings, Dodgers GM Brandon Gomes said none of his conversations since arriving in Las Vegas had painted a clear picture of how the free agent or trade markets might play out this month.
 The Dodgers are going to take a “business as usual” approach to the offseason, prepared to react whenever those markets reveal themselves. But even if Gomes and president of baseball operations Andrew Freidman aren’t ready to predict how the threat of a lockout — expected to go into effect when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1 — will affect their offseason, it surely will color this transaction window.
 The Dodgers don’t have any gaping holes to fill this winter, but they still need to fortify their roster if they hope to reclaim their spot at the top of the league.
 Advertisement The Dodgers already hired former Miami Marlins hitting coach Pedro Guerrero to fill the only opening on their coaching staff, and made their first offseason acquisition, claiming infielder Christian Cairo off waivers from the New York Mets on Monday.
 Dodgers 
 Dodgers hire former Marlins coach Pedro Guerrero as new hitting instructor 
 The Dodgers hire Pedro Guerrero, who spent two seasons as the Miami Marlins hitting coach, before the team decided not to retain him for the 2027 season.
 Nov. 10, 2026 Their most pressing needs are their bullpen and bench, areas that often draw less fanfare. But the Dodgers also have a track record of splashy offseason moves.
 Here are takeaways from Gomes’ media availability Tuesday:
 Dodgers engaged with Tarik Skubal’s camp
 Tarik Skubal during Game 1 of the NLCS. (Ashley Landis / AP) Advertisement As Freidman said they would, the Dodgers have remained in contact with southpaw Tarik Skubal ’s camp, Gomes confirmed. And they expect to have a meeting “at some point,” he said.
 Skubal is the top free agent and is sure to garner interest from all the heavy hitters. The Mets have a meeting scheduled with him next week, according to reports.
 The Dodgers’ pitch started when they acquired him at the trade deadline But it’s unclear just how aggressive they will be in pursuit of a reunion.
 “A lot of it is continuing to see what this all looks like,” Gomes said. “He was awesome getting to know. He fit in great into the clubhouse. Obviously, we know what kind of pitcher he is. So for us, it’s understanding what this all looks like, as far as what does our team need? What does the contract look like? Where does he end up? I don’t know.
 “We know we love the player, we love the human, and you kind of have to let things play out to understand what that looks like, and if it’s something that we’re gonna ultimately execute.”
 Japanese phenom Shoki Oda on the Dodgers’ radar
 Oda, 18, plans to go straight from high school baseball in Japan to the United States, foregoing a stint in Nippon Professional Baseball. He’s begun meeting with major-league teams.
 Advertisement “He’s super talented, really projectable, fun to watch him throw,” Gomes said. “I know our international guys have watched him closely, and you know, I’m not sure how that all shakes out exactly. But we think really highly of him.”
 Asked whether Oda had visited with the Dodgers, Gomes said with a smile: “Potentially.”
 Dodgers looking for Miguel Rojas replacement
 Who can fill Miguel Rojas’ shoes? (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) Rojas already has begun the transition into his player development role with the Dodgers, working with prospects in the Arizona Fall League. But now the Dodgers have to fill the hole his retirement left on the roster.
 New addition Cairo adds depth to the infield group and like Rojas is a right-handed hitter.
 “He has really good bat-to-ball [skills], good defensively in a bunch of different spots,” Gomes said. “Our scouts have flagged him as somebody that they really liked, and makeup was really strong.”
 Veteran utility player Kiké Hernández also entered free agency. In a similar situation last year, the Dodgers brought him back on a one-year deal.
 Advertisement “Kiké’s been such a huge part of what we’ve done in the past, and we’ll continue to have those conversations,” Gomes said. “But what that looks like right now, I have no idea.”
 At the beginning of the season, with switch-hitting utility player Tommy Edman on the injured list, the Dodgers had two young second basemen competing for the left-handed-hitting side of the platoon. Alex Freeland won the job, and Hyeseong Kim, in his second year of a three-year contract worth $12.5 million, made nearly three quarters of his plate appearances in triple A.
 “Comet did not have the year that he was expecting offensively, but he has so many skills that fit us well,” Gomes said of Kim. “Diving in this offseason, to continue to chip away at the potential swing changes, and he worked on some stuff at the end of the year that he felt pretty good about after presenting a plan. He’ll continue to work through those things and hopefully he’ll take a step forward on the swing mechanics and get him into a really good place offensively.”
 Important offseason for Josue De Paula
 Josue De Paula warms up before Game 2 of the NLDS. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) De Paula not only proved that his offensive skills were major league-ready last season, but also earned a spot on the postseason roster with a mature approach in high-pressure situations.
 For him to claim a regular role next year, however, he’ll have to continue to progress on defense.
 Advertisement “He is dead set on proving that he’s going to be a really good defender,” Gomes said. “And he has a good setup in the offseason with people around him that he’s going to go out and you know really get after it. And we have full confidence that he’s going to put the work in to really continue to take those steps forward and be the complete player that we all know he can be.”
 The potential lockout would add another wrinkle. Because he’s on the 40-man roster, the Dodgers wouldn’t be able to communicate with him during the lockout, as he works through his offseason program.
 “We’re going to make sure that we’re set up in a way over this next month to continue to communicate with guys like we we normally do,” Gomes said. “And if things shake out in a way that we can’t, we’ll make sure that those conversations on the front end are had to kind of put everybody on the same page moving forward.”
